extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how and when USPTO examiners should reject patent claims (prior art and non‑prior art grounds), the required content and form of rejections, rules for final rejections, and special circumstances (e.g., previously allowed claims, claims copied from patents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art rejections (35 U.S.C. §§ 102, 103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejection ground for lack of novelty (§102) or obviousness (§103); the most common ground for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must conduct thorough prior art searching, 'cite the best references at his or her command,' and clearly explain the pertinence of cited references when that pertinence is not apparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑prior art rejections (706.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejections based on statutory or other non‑prior art grounds, including lack of utility (35 U.S.C. §107), ineligible subject matter (35 U.S.C. §101), inadequate written description or enablement (35 U.S.C. §112), double patenting, and improper Markush groupings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must provide a 'full development of the reasons' supporting such rejections rather than mere conclusory statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unequivocal language and designation of relied parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejection language must be 'unequivocal' and must clearly state all grounds of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should designate 'the particular part relied on as nearly as practicable' so that the applicant can understand the basis for the rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required elements of a proper rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Each rejection must: specify which claims are rejected; clearly explain each ground of rejection; cite supporting references when applicable; and, when practicable, indicate how the rejections might be overcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These elements ensure the applicant can meaningfully respond; failure to include them can render the action defective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for making final rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rejection may be made on the second or subsequent examination, subject to limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A final rejection is improper if the examiner introduces new grounds not necessitated by claim amendments or by information disclosure statements filed with required fees. Before making a final rejection, a 'clear issue should be developed between the examiner and applicant,' and the examiner must repeat all applicable grounds and clearly state supporting reasons. Final actions must include the appropriate form paragraphs (7.39–7.42) notifying applicants of appeal rights and options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premature final rejection (procedural constraint)
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions about the prematureness of a final rejection must be raised while the application is pending before the primary examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determinations about prematureness are procedural and are reviewable only by petition, not by appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special care when rejecting previously allowed claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When rejecting a claim that was previously marked allowable, 'great care should be exercised.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only primary examiners may make such rejections, and the Office action must include form paragraph 7.50 to notify applicants of the prior allowability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling claims copied from existing patents
rubrics_metrics.description: When claims are copied from existing patents, the examiner must determine whether corresponding patent claims are also unpatentable under the asserted grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the rejection ground would also render the patent's claims unpatentable, the Office action must be approved by the Technology Center Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive treatment of form defects
rubrics_metrics.description: For defects in form, examiners should make 'constructive' rejections rather than bare objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should offer a definite suggestion for correction so the applicant can remedy the defect, instead of issuing bare form objections without guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform application of patentability requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentability requirements must be applied uniformly across all art areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The standard of proof for rejection is the 'preponderance of the evidence'—i.e., the examiner should reject claims 'if, in view of the prior art and evidence of record, it is more likely than not that the claim is unpatentable.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing and explaining references when pertinence is not apparent
rubrics_metrics.description: When the relevance of a cited reference to a claim is not obvious, the examiner must explain why the reference is pertinent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is part of the examiner's duty to 'cite the best references' and to communicate clear reasoning so applicants can respond effectively.
